structure: Part 12 read the set's composition seam and rule manifest in full: set.js (set id and base), routes.js and routes-high-risk-plants.js (the set plugin: set context, obligation set, fulfilment registry, journey flow, readiness, purity and coverage asserts, dispatch, stores, cookie, entry guard, route table, completeness check), src/server/router.js (mount under /high-risk-plants behind auth.enabled, root redirect), features/index.js (13 dispatch pages, 18 route modules, 40 routes), evaluation.js (10 feature bindings), timing-windows.js (2 windows), obligations/index.js and its seven section files (25 obligations, 1 group: commodityLines), whitelists.test.js and coverage.test.js (manifest invariants and the two exceptions: quantity ungated, seed potatoes unconstrained), amend-endings.test.js (3 tests), and the three cross-page fit specs: type-ahead (18 tests, 34 runs over origin, place of landing and genus), section-caption (2) and page-title (2). For route registration only it read the page.js and controller route tables of every feature, paths.js, kit.js pageRoutes and CANCEL_AMEND_SLUG, parties/index.js edit slugs, picker-routes.js, notification-action-slugs.js and fulfilment-registry.js. Every route is claimed once here; page content belongs to parts 1 to 11. Since the earlier extract (a88175f) only kit.js and fulfilment-registry.js line numbers moved in this slice; no route, obligation or spec changed.

claims.statement: One notification-level place of destination is owed for every commodity type, and it is never behind a gate; which of the three sentences a notifier sees is the page's business, decided from the arrival status.

claims.statement: Every request to the set is checked by the journey entry guard before the page runs, and a request that fails it is redirected away rather than served.
The set refuses to start if any of its configuration seams is unfilled or any of its journey cookies is unregistered, so a misconfigured journey fails at boot rather than serving half a journey.
claims.quote:
* Refuse to mount a set that has not configured every required seam or
 * registered every journey cookie.
claims.note: mechanism: checks the set's own registration against the seam registry and the Hapi server's cookie states at mount time; it works on configuration, not on a notification's data.

claims.note: Collected by the identification-numbers page.

claims.statement: A producer identification number is required only when the notification is for potatoes.
claims.note: Collected by the identification-numbers page.

claims.note: Collected by the identification-numbers page.

claims.statement: A consignor is required only for plants for planting and for wood and cut trees, and a potato notification is never asked for one.

claims.statement: Every notification must say what is being imported — its commodity type — and the question applies whatever the answer.
claims.note: Collected by the commodity-type page; every other commodity-type gate in the manifest reads this one answer.

claims.statement: A notification must carry at least one commodity line, and a notification with no line at all is refused with the code obligation.commodityLines.atLeastOne.
claims.note: This is the manifest's one cardinality rule, and its one group: it is always in scope and is collected by the commodities list.

claims.statement: The commodity lines are a group that is always in scope, and a notification holding no line satisfies it vacuously as far as the fields below it are concerned.
Every commodity line must say which category it is, and that answer decides which of the other per-line questions the line is asked.
claims.note: Collected by the commodities feature, whose bindings own the ten per-line leaves.

claims.statement: Every commodity line must carry a quantity, whichever category it is, and it is the one per-line field with no category condition.

Genus, species, commodity code, potato variety, potato intended use, EPPO code, size of tree and phytosanitary treatments are each required on a commodity line only when the line's category asks for that field, and the list of categories that ask for it comes from the set's own commodity service rather than the manifest.
claims.quote:
const gatedOnCategory = (id, name) => ({
  id,
  name,
  within: commodityLine,
  status: 'mandatory',
  applyTo: allowListed(
    category,
    () => categoriesRequiring(name),
    null,
    appliesBecauseCategory(name)
  )
})

Each is mandatory within commodityLine. All eight, with category and quantity, are collected by the commodities feature.

claims.statement: Each per-line field's reason for applying is recorded in the words "<field> applies on lines whose category asks for it", under the code obligation.<field>.applicable.becauseCategory.
Which categories ask for a per-line field is looked up only when the rule is checked, so the manifest reads no reference data when the service starts.
claims.quote:
* A per-line field scoped to the categories the set-owned service says ask for
 * it. The allow-list is read lazily, at gate execution: an obligation module
 * does no IO and reads no reference data when it loads.

claims.statement: A notification carries one country of origin for the whole consignment, whatever its commodity type, and must give it.
claims.note: Id 5e18b2b2-06d3-49af-a55c-b78013d284c0, status mandatory, no applyTo. Collected by the origin page.

claims.statement: Which countries a particular category may come from — ware potatoes from four countries, conifer wood without bark from four others, everything else from an EU member State — is checked on the origin page against the set's own commodity service, not by the manifest's rules, because the category sits on each commodity line while the origin is one answer for the notification.
Whether the consignment has already arrived in Great Britain is asked only of notifications for plants for planting and for wood and cut trees.
claims.quote:
explanation:
      'arrivalStatus applies to notifications for plants for planting and for wood and cut trees'
claims.note: Id 6f29c3c3-17e4-45b0-b66d-c89124e395d1, status mandatory, includesGate on commodityType with the reason code obligation.arrivalStatus.applicable.becauseCommodityType. Collected by the arrival-status page.

claims.statement: The notifier says whether the consignment has arrived rather than the service working it out from the arrival date, because one branch of the rules turns on arrival in the country and the other on arrival at the destination, and a date alone cannot tell them apart.
claims.quote:
* The notifier says so rather than the service deriving it from the arrival
 * date: reg 26(2)(a) branches on arrival in the country and reg 26(2)(b) on
 * arrival at the intended destination, and a date alone cannot say which
 * branch a consignment arriving today is in.

claims.statement: When a change of commodity type takes the arrival status out of scope, the answer already given is removed rather than kept.
claims.quote:
* A top-level scalar gate on a top-level scalar answer, so the whole
 * notification is either asked the question or not — the engine purges the
 * answer when a change of commodity type takes it out of scope.

claims.statement: Every notification must give an arrival date, whatever its commodity type, and the three different ways the question is worded are a matter for the arrival-details page, not for the rule.
claims.quote:
* One obligation for every commodity type, because every notification owes a
 * date: reg 24A(2)(a) asks potatoes for the expected date, and reg 26(2)(a)
 * asks plants and wood for the expected date of landing or, once the
 * consignment is here, the date it first arrived. Which of those three
 * sentences a notifier is shown is the arrival-details page's business — the
 * matter owed is the same one.
claims.note: Id 63e22d64-b9a0-40b4-aec6-0f5f48bdd556, status mandatory, no applyTo. Collected by the arrival-details page.

claims.statement: An expected time of arrival is asked only of potato notifications, and the answer is removed if the notification changes to another commodity type.
claims.quote:
* Reg 24A(2)(a) asks potatoes for 'the expected time and date of their
 * arrival'. Reg 26(2)(a) asks plants and wood for a date alone, so the time is
 * a potato matter and the engine purges it when a notification changes to
 * another commodity type.
claims.note: Id 0d05c100-b887-4a12-8251-673bc1e1ac31, status mandatory, equalsGate on commodityType = potatoes, reason code obligation.arrivalTime.applicable.becauseCommodityType with the words 'arrivalTime applies to notifications for potatoes'. Collected by the arrival-details page.

claims.statement: A proposed place of landing is asked only of potato notifications; plants and wood are never asked for one.
claims.quote:
* Reg 24A(2)(aa) is the only landing element in the statute; reg 26(2) has
 * none, so plants and wood are never asked. Gated the same way as the time, on
 * the same notification-level answer.
claims.note: Id 1c706e7c-6d61-4e47-8bb4-e53efcd72809, status mandatory, equalsGate on commodityType = potatoes, reason code obligation.proposedPlaceOfLanding.applicable.becauseCommodityType with the words 'proposedPlaceOfLanding applies to notifications for potatoes'. Collected by the arrival-details page.

claims.statement: Every notification must give one place of destination — where the consignment is going, or where it is being kept once it is here — and which of those three questions the notifier is shown is decided from the arrival status by the page, not by the rule.
claims.note: Id 7eb0d717-f852-43f7-9377-c6a9c301d702, status mandatory, no applyTo. Collected by the place-of-destination picker.

claims.statement: The place of destination a notification holds is a copy of the organisation's address-book record taken when it was picked, and a later change to that record does not reach the notification.
claims.quote:

claims.statement: The commodity lines are the manifest's only group, and the set of groups is worked out from what the other obligations sit within rather than listed by hand.
claims.note: coverage.test.js checks the derived groups by identity, so a hand-written stand-in for the commodity-line group fails: 'a hand-written copy of a group object would pass a structural comparison and then fail every `within === group` test the evaluator makes'.

claims.statement: No two obligations may share an id or a name, because a duplicate would make one of them silently invisible to the service and corrupt every lookup by name.
claims.quote:
// Duplicate ids collide in every id-keyed structure the evaluator builds;
    // one wins and the loser is silently invisible.

claims.statement: Each constrained category is answered from the one constraint that binds it, and the constraint lists cannot be added to at runtime.
The arrival status question is admitted for exactly two commodity types, plants for planting and wood and cut trees, and for no other value the service offers.

The pair of commodity types that get the post-arrival branch is written out rather than worked out, so a new commodity type the service starts offering is not asked the arrival status until someone decides it should be.
The arrival time and the proposed place of landing are each admitted for potatoes and nothing else, and both read the commodity type answer.
The consignor question reads the commodity type answer and is admitted for plants for planting and wood and cut trees only.
Every question the notification owes is collected by exactly one page: the service refuses to start and names the offenders when any of them is collected by none.
claims.note: This is the coverage invariant for the manifest, checked at boot by assertFulfilmentBindingCoverage() against the set's featureEvaluationBindings. The only exception is a group: a group obligation is not a leaf, so the commodity-line group needs no collecting page.

Between them the ten features own all 24 leaf obligations — review 1, contact 1, identification numbers 4, commodity type 1, commodities 10, origin 1, arrival status 1, arrival details 3, place of destination 1 and consignor 1.

claims.statement: An amendment ends every task-row page with exactly the controls that page shows on a draft, so nothing is added or taken away just because the notification is being amended.
claims.note: The test runs over every page of every task row, taken from taskRows.flatMap((row) => row.pages).

claims.statement: A question page offers two buttons, Save and continue and Save and return to overview, followed by a link that cancels back to the overview.
claims.quote: it('Should offer Save and continue, Save and return to overview and a link to cancel back to the overview', async () => {
claims.note: The second button submits `value="hub" name="exit"`, and the link points at the notification's hub path. The words come from the shared saveActions copy keys saveAndContinue, saveAndReturnToHub and cancelAndReturnToHub.

claims.statement: Every page carries a section caption immediately above its heading, as the element directly before the h1 rather than text elsewhere on the page.
claims.note: The caption is a govuk-caption-xl span and the heading a govuk-heading-xl h1.

claims.statement: The notification list is captioned "Dashboard" above the heading "Import notification service".
claims.quote: dashboard: 'Dashboard',
claims.note: The heading text comes from the dashboard copy's `title: 'Import notification service'`.

claims.statement: A captioned page has no serious or critical accessibility violations.
claims.quote: test('has no serious or critical axe violations with a caption on the page', async ({

claims.statement: A page's browser title reads the page name, then the service name, then GOV.UK, joined by hyphens: for example "What are you importing? - Import notification service - GOV.UK".
claims.note: serviceName is 'Import notification service', govukSuffix is 'GOV.UK', and the commodity type page's title is 'What are you importing?'.

claims.statement: When a page comes back showing errors, its browser title is prefixed "Error: " in front of the whole title.
claims.note: errorTitlePrefix is 'Error: '.

claims.statement: Three questions are answered with a search box that suggests as the user types: the country of origin, the proposed place of landing and a commodity line's genus.
claims.quote:
const typeAheads = [
  {
    name: 'Country of origin',
    inputId: 'countryOfOrigin',
claims.note: The other two entries are named 'Proposed place of landing' (inputId proposedPlaceOfLanding) and 'Commodity details genus' (inputId genus). Eight of the spec's eighteen tests run against each of the three, so 24 of its 34 runs are these three pages checked alike.

claims.statement: Each search box opens empty and carries its page's own placeholder: "Search for a country" on the origin page, "Select a place of landing" on the arrival details page, and none on the genus field.
claims.quote:
await expect(input).toHaveAttribute('placeholder', searchPlaceholder)
      await expect(input).toHaveValue('')
claims.note: searchPlaceholder values: originCopy.country.searchPlaceholder = 'Search for a country', arrivalCopy.placeOfLanding.searchPlaceholder = 'Select a place of landing', and the genus entry sets `searchPlaceholder: ''`.

claims.statement: A search box shows a square button flush with the right-hand edge of the box, top and bottom aligned with it, and shows no dropdown arrow.
claims.quote: test('shows a square button flush with the right of the box and no dropdown arrow', async ({

claims.statement: The search button is hidden from assistive technology and from the tab order, and clicking it only moves focus into the box without leaving the page.
claims.quote: test('keeps the button out of assistive technology and the tab order, and focuses the box when it is clicked', async ({
claims.note: The button is a span carrying aria-hidden="true" and no tabindex, and the page URL is unchanged after the click.

claims.statement: A suggestion shows the letters the user typed in bold: typing "fra" bolds "Fra" in France, "dov" bolds "Dov" in Port of Dover - GB DVR, and "cast" bolds "Cast" in Castanea.
claims.quote: test(`shows ${bold} in bold in the ${suggestion} suggestion after typing ${typed}`, async ({

claims.statement: Accents do not have to match: typing "Dóv" suggests Port of Dover and typing "Cást" suggests Castanea, each with the unaccented letters bolded, and typing an accented name such as Réunion matches the accented entry.
claims.quote: test(`shows ${accentedBold} in bold in the ${accentedSuggestion} suggestion after typing ${accentedTyped}`, async ({
claims.note: The origin entry's accented case types 'Réunion' and expects the FR-LRE entry's whole name bolded.

claims.statement: A page with a search box has no serious or critical accessibility violations, with the button showing and with a suggestion list open.
claims.quote: test('has no serious or critical axe violations with a suggestion list open', async ({

claims.statement: Without JavaScript each of the three questions is a plain select found by its own label, whose first option is the page's own prompt with no value, with no search button, no suggestion list and nothing hidden from assistive technology.
claims.quote: test('is a native select found by its label, sized as a GOV.UK label of its size, whose first option is the page select text, with no button', async ({
claims.note: The first option's text is the page's selectText — 'Select a country', 'Select a place of landing' and 'Select a genus' — and its value is the empty string.

claims.statement: The country of origin and proposed place of landing labels are medium-sized GOV.UK labels, and the genus label is small.
claims.quote: await expectGovukLabelSize(page, formGroup.locator('label'), labelSize)
claims.note: labelSize is 'm' for countryOfOrigin and proposedPlaceOfLanding and 's' for genus.

claims.statement: Each search box is described by its field's hint, and a field with no hint has no description: the hints are "Select where the potatoes will enter Great Britain. Start typing to search by port or airport name or code." for the place of landing and "Start typing to search for a genus." for the genus.
claims.quote: await expect(select).toHaveAccessibleDescription(hint ?? '')
claims.note: The country of origin entry declares no hint, so its description is empty. Hint wording read from arrival-details and commodities copy.en.js.

claims.statement: Choosing a country announces the change exactly once, whether the suggestion is clicked, chosen with Enter after arrowing down, or settled by leaving the box on an exact match, and the underlying answer is set to that country's code.
claims.note: Three tests, one per way of choosing; each asserts exactly one change event and the native select holding the chosen code.

claims.statement: The country search box is described to a screen reader as "When autocomplete results are available use up and down arrows to review and enter to select. Touch device users, explore by touch or with swipe gestures."
claims.quote:
const assistiveHint =
      'When autocomplete results are available use up and down arrows to review and enter to select. Touch device users, explore by touch or with swipe gestures.'

claims.statement: Typing in the country box announces how many results are available, such as "1 result is available.", and arrowing onto one announces it with its place among them, such as "Iceland 1 of 1 is highlighted".
claims.quote: await expect(statusRegion(page, '1 result is available.')).toHaveCount(1)
claims.note: The announcement is read from one of two status regions, #countryOfOrigin__status--A or #countryOfOrigin__status--B, and the highlight announcement is asserted as `1 result is available. ${iceland.name} 1 of 1 is highlighted`.

claims.statement: The notification list's start button reads "Start a new notification", and pressing it opens the commodity type question, whose heading and legend are "What are you importing?".
claims.note: dashboardCopy.startButton is 'Start a new notification' and commodityTypeCopy.legend is 'What are you importing?'.

claims.statement: Every page of the journey requires a signed-in user: all three cross-page specs sign in before they can reach a page.

The caption pattern is proven on the notification list alone: no spec in this part asserts the caption above the heading of any collecting page, so what caption each journey section shows is not held to by a cross-page test.
claims.note: Looked in section-caption.fit.spec.js, which has two tests and both start at the set base; the section captions module itself and its copy are read by another part.

claims.statement: The title pattern is proven on the commodity type page alone: no spec in this part asserts the title of the hub, the notification list, check your answers, the declaration or the confirmation.
claims.note: Looked in page-title.fit.spec.js, whose two tests both begin at the commodity type page.

claims.statement: The three cross-page specs assert English copy only: none of them checks the Welsh caption, title or search-box wording, although every feature keeps a copy.cy.js beside its copy.en.js.
claims.note: Looked at every copy import in the three specs: all are copy.en.js. Whether the Welsh copy exists and what it says is another part's claim.

claims.statement: Nothing in the obligation manifest says how long an answer is allowed to be, what characters it may hold or what its error message says: the manifest carries only ids, names, statuses, groups and conditions.
claims.note: Looked at all seven section files and the index. The only message-like values are the reason codes and explanations on the gates and the commodity-line errorCode. Field-level validation and its wording live with each page, which other parts claim.
